heading: Negative heads across tasks and models share the same copy-suppression role
definition: negative heads in narrow tasks (e.g. negative name movers in IOI) and in other models and sizes are instances of the same copy-suppression role.
summary: Several independent groups report copy-suppression-like behavior in other tasks and models. Opposite signs, domain specialization and increased confidence in toy models weaken the claim that all share the same role.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: R2 (GPT-2-small IOI NNM group, arXiv:2608.19338; Pythia-160m/410m IOI, arXiv:2407.10827, which has an opposite-sign limit). 1-10B: R2 with limits (Pythia-1.4b/2.8b IOI, arXiv:2407.10827; Pythia-6.9B CounterFact heads, arXiv:2402.11655 and arXiv:2507.11809, domain-specialized; Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 at layer level only, arXiv:2502.20475). Toy: R0 (one study, arXiv:2501.18666, where the function differs). 10-100B and >100B: no tests (counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size has no such key).
suggested_status.reason:
Counts: versions.V5.verdicts.supports.studies = 6, limits_scope.studies = 3, challenges.studies = 0; versions.V5.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0.

What other groups reproduce:
- In GPT-2-small IOI, the negative name mover group suppresses the IO name, and this depends on the upstream copiers (ablation with 95% CIs, arXiv:2608.19338).
- Copy-suppression-like heads in Pythia: arXiv:2407.10827, arXiv:2402.11655, arXiv:2507.11809.
- Suppression of in-context, already-promoted tokens by late attention layers in Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (arXiv:2502.20475).

Where 'the same role' is weaker:
- Only the original reports a partial QK weights test in another pretrained model: the experiment is repeated in GPT-2 Medium and compared with IOI direct logit attribution. No corresponding GPT-2 Medium OV weights analysis or full mechanistic confirmation is reported (arXiv:2310.04625#r18).
- In Pythia IOI, the CS heads have the opposite sign and negative name movers are a separate class (arXiv:2407.10827).
- The Pythia-6.9B heads are domain-specialized (arXiv:2507.11809).
- In toy models, the copy-suppression-like head raises confidence (arXiv:2501.18666#r4).

So R2 fits 'copy-suppression-like suppression appears in other models and narrow tasks'. The identity claim ('instances of the same role') has less support.
suggested_status.open_questions:
- A QK/OV weights comparison showing that Pythia, Llama or Mistral heads match L10H7's mechanism would firm up R2 for 'same role'.
- Head-level localization in Llama or Mistral.
- An explanation of the opposite sign in Pythia IOI. If those heads play a different role, the version needs narrowing, and a credible argument to that effect would move the 'same role' part toward C.
- A per-head retest of 10.7 and 11.10 in IOI by a group other than the original's.
- Any test above 10B.

source.title: Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding a Motif in Language Model Attention Heads
source.authors: Callum McDougall; Arthur Conmy; Cody Rushing; Thomas McGrath; Neel Nanda

original_result.setup: They compared anti-induction and IOI copy-suppression scores and applied a QK-circuit test to GPT-2 Medium.
original_result.result: L10H7 ranked highest for copy suppression and negative induction in GPT-2 Small; in GPT-2 Medium, the two most prominently recovered heads were two of the three most negative IOI heads. Pythia showed weaker instances, and the scores correlated strongly where both were positive across GPT, Pythia and SoLU.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Pythia factual heads attended to counterfactual tokens, resembling GPT-2's proposed suppression mechanism.
Copy-suppression heads appeared across all tested Pythia IOI circuits after circuit emergence.
Late attention layers suppressed previously generated answers in Llama and Mistral factual recall.
GPT-2 negative name movers suppressed copied names more strongly when primary copiers were present.
Amplified Pythia factual heads suppressed factual tokens already stated in prompts.
Toy sorting models developed vocabulary-wide suppression heads with query–key structure resembling copying heads.
Pythia copy-suppression heads and negative IOI heads formed different sets.
Pythia suppression heads showed domain specialization across answer categories.
Toy sorting suppression raised confidence, while its structure varied with training conditions.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Weights-level (QK/OV) evidence, from any group other than the original and in any pretrained model, that negative heads elsewhere share L10H7's mechanism. What exists is the original's partial QK test in GPT-2 Medium (arXiv:2310.04625#r18) and toy-model circuits (arXiv:2501.18666).
untested.basis: The untested lines of arXiv:2310.04625 (the authors say they lack mechanistic confirmation in other models and sizes), arXiv:2507.11809 (no comparison showing the Pythia heads share L10H7's QK/OV mechanism) and arXiv:2502.20475. counts: versions.V5.main_rows_by_operation lists only measurement, removal, evaluation and other.
counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size has only the keys 'not stated', '1-10B' and '<1B'.

untested.what: Head-level localization of suppression in Llama, Mistral, other families beyond GPT-2 and Pythia, and instruct/chat models.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V5.studies_by_family (GPT-2, Pythia, Llama, other or not stated) and versions.V5.studies_by_stage (instruct/chat: 1). The only instruct evidence is layer-level (verdict notes on arXiv:2502.20475#R1 and #R3; untested line of arXiv:2502.20475).

wording_issues.phrase: negative heads in narrow tasks (e.g. negative name movers in IOI) ... are instances of the same copy-suppression role
wording_issues.issue: In Pythia IOI, the heads classified as copy suppression (CSPA >10%) contribute positively by downweighting the repeated subject name, the opposite sign from GPT-2's. In Pythia-160m, the negative name mover (9.1) is classified separately from the CS heads 8.9 (positive) and 9.5 (negative). So in this family the negative IOI heads and the CS heads are different sets. Text-based verdict, no row.

In Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, suppression of previous answers is shown only for summed whole-layer attention output, with no head localized (verdict notes on R1, R3). In GPT-2-small IOI, the independent ablation evidence is group-level: 10.7 and 11.10 are ablated together (problems line of arXiv:2608.19338).

In the two-head toy list-sorter, entropy increases after either head is ablated (r4). The suppressing head therefore increases confidence, reversing V3's confidence direction; entropy alone cannot determine V5's identity of role (cannot_determine). The authors name its parallel placement and the missing MLP as differences from GPT-2. In GPT-2 small, the reported role of head 10.7 changes across Simple, Opposite and Complex syllogism formats (method-sensitivity line of arXiv:2508.16109). The original itself reports a Stanford GPT-2 Small E head that self-repairs in IOI but, unlike GPT-2 small's CS heads, attends equally to IO and S2 (App. Q, not-in-rows line).

In Pythia-6.9B, the suppressor heads are domain-specialized: L20H18 has negligible effect on some answer categories and encodes location and language tokens (text-based limits_scope). The original reports weaker instances in Pythia (r19, partial). In GPT-2 Medium it reports only a partial QK-circuit test, which the verdict fix describes as a QK-circuit weights test plus IOI direct logit attribution (r18). Its cross-class evidence (GPT, Pythia, SoLU) is a correlation between anti-induction and CS scores within a quadrant, with no coefficient stated (r20). No V5 test exists above 10B (counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size).

method_sensitivity.what: In GPT-2-small IOI, magnitudes shift with ablation type but the direction and interaction ordering do not. Δ(E) is −2.270 (mean) vs −2.335 (zero) (r1, r2), and I_PE 1.830 vs 1.681 (r3, r4). The not-in-rows lines give Δ(P+E) of −0.136 (mean) vs −0.769 (zero), and a B×E interaction of 0.502 [0.429, 0.576] (mean) vs 0.518 [0.416, 0.618] (zero). The paper says the ordering persists across eight lexical/order conditions and both ablations. The held-out predictive comparison uses one template and mean ablation only.

method_sensitivity.factor: Attention amplification strength (alpha), sentence structure and answer category
method_sensitivity.what: In Pythia-6.9B, factual output varies with alpha and falls below 70% at alpha=10 on factual prompts (r3; Sec. 4.3.2). Head contributions vary by answer category: L20H18 has negligible effect on some categories (Sec. 4.4.2). Sentence-structure dependence of the best alpha is reported for GPT-2 robustness experiments: alpha 10 performs better for matching sentence structures, alpha 5 for differing structures (Secs. 4.2.1–4.2.2). This dependence is not established for Pythia-6.9B.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training-data gap distribution and head count (toy)
method_sensitivity.what: In toy one-layer attention-only list-sorting transformers, whether copy suppression emerges depends on the mean and variance of δ. Allowed-gap datasets with δ variance 7.6–10.5 end in copy suppression; lower-variance allowed-gap datasets give one-head sorting. In a 4-head model, head 2 exhibits copy suppression at an intermediate training stage (r6, observed), and the arrangement changes during training; the later prose does not establish whether head 2's suppressive role persists. On perturbed training data, the QK circuits differ, and identity with the usual copy-suppression mode is not established (r7).
In GPT-2 small, the reported role of head 10.7 changes across the Simple, Opposite and Complex Syllogism formats. The V5-linked row is from Complex Syllogism only (r5).

In Pythia 160m–2.8b IOI circuits, copy-suppression component scores vary in emergence speed and strength across sizes and checkpoints (Sec. 3.2, Fig. 2). The curves are normalised, so magnitudes cannot be compared (cspa rows cannot_determine). The every-checkpoint sampling for 160m and approximately one-third sampling for larger models apply to post-emergence algorithm-verification metrics (Sec. 4.2, Fig. 4B–D), not to the CSPA component-score curves.

method_sensitivity.factor: Sample selection, metric and score region (original baseline)
method_sensitivity.what: The original reports that its results depend on the behavioural sample (the top 5% by L10H7 effect), on KL-divergence versus loss-based metrics, and on an idealized versus a more faithful input approximation. Its cross-model anti-induction/CS association is stated for the quadrant where both scores are positive, with no coefficient (r20). The accompanying post's row says the same (lw r4, NOT A TEST).
